method: Every fetched_url re-fetched (archive.org full-text search-inside endpoint for brown-1959 dli.csl.8666, ganguly-1912 in.ernet.dli.2015.536395, panigrahi-1961 in.ernet.dli.2015.111041, fergusson-1876 in.ernet.dli.2015.62030). All four are complete scans downloadable on archive.org, so confirmed quotes count as full-text. Mitra 1880 (mitra-r-1880, in.ernet.dli.2015.44126) was searched separately for the height. Locators give the archive.org OCR leaf; printed pages were NOT checked. OCR errors tolerated in matching.

rulings.facts.height: UNCERTAIN, value_m 65.4. Four figures: Ganguly 1912 reports his own theodolite survey, 214.67 ft (65.4 m) from road level to the top of the stone finial (209.42 ft from the Uttara-parsva Math compound, which he gives as 5 ft 3 in above the road) (leaves 502-503). Fergusson 1876: 192 ft (leaf 442). Mitra 1880: 'The Puri temple, with a base of 80 feet square, has a height of 192 feet' (leaf 229; leaf 226 also 'raised from 160 to 192 feet'). Brown 1959: 'nearly 200 feet' (leaf 215). Spread 58.5-65.4 m, much narrower than Lingaraja's 39-55 m (which was nulled). Ganguly's is the only figure with a stated measuring method, so it is the display value, but the text and note state the lower figures; tier uncertain; not an ASI measurement. 226 ft and 229 ft: no accepted source, left out. If the human prefers the Lingaraja approach (null), set facts.height and sections.size.height_m to null.
rulings.facts.date: UNCERTAIN, value 'late 11th–12th century CE', sort_year 1100. Brown: c. 1100, 'records' of consecration in 1118. Ganguly: within Chodaganga's reign, 1075-1145. Panigrahi: 12th century under Chodaganga. Fergusson: soon after 1131. The research report's '1112 CE start' is not in any source seen (pitfalls.md).
rulings.patron: facts.dynasty = Chodaganga (scholarly). The Anangabhima tradition goes to sections.construction as a separate uncertain claim. 'Completed under Anangabhima III' is not in any source seen and is not published; Panigrahi says only 'his successor Anangabhima in the twelfth century' and dates Anangabhima II to 1190-1198.
rulings.temple_type (top-level): Set to 'rekha' because the validator requires rekha|pidha|khakhara. No fetched Puri passage uses the word 'rekha'; Ganguly calls the tower a 'pancharatha dewl' with 9 bhumis. The facts.temple_type claim says only 'pancharatha deul'.
rulings.parts.element_ids: jagamohana, natamandira, bhogamandapa (all in research/staged/elements-names.json). bada/gandi/mastaka/pista not added: no fetched passage names them for the Puri tower.
rulings.sensitive: 023 (Buddhist origin of the images / tooth-relic site) and 022 (Panigrahi on the cult drawing on Buddhism, Jainism and 'primitive cults') touch the origin of a living faith: needs-human, not staged.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaves 214-215 ('about A.D, 1100', 'not consecrated until A.D. 1118'), Ganguly leaf 486 (1075-76 to c. 1145), Panigrahi leaf 277 ('twelfth century'), Fergusson leaf 440 ('In 1131') all found. Value changed from 'c. 1075–1150 CE' (1150 not in any source) to 'late 11th–12th century CE'. Fergusson kept in note only. Brown's '1030 A.D.' conquest date not published.
verdicts.revised_text: The present temple was built in the late 11th or the 12th century CE. Scholars give different years for it.

verdicts.reason: Panigrahi leaf 282, Ganguly leaf 486, Fergusson leaf 440 found. 'Eastern Ganga' is not the sources' wording; changed to 'Ganga dynasty' (as in the Konark page). Copper-plates reported by Ganguly, not opened: scholarly.
verdicts.revised_text: It was built by kings of the Ganga dynasty. Historians name King Anantavarman Chodaganga as the builder of the present temple.

verdicts.reason: Ganguly leaves 485, 488 and Panigrahi leaf 47 found. 'arranged its worship' is not in any quote seen; removed. Anangabhima left unnumbered. Placed in sections.construction.
verdicts.revised_text: According to popular tradition, King Anangabhima built the temple. Historians M.M. Ganguly and K.C. Panigrahi credit Chodaganga, with Anangabhima adding to it later.

verdicts.reason: Ganguly leaves 502-503 (theodolite; '= 214-67 ft.'; 209-42 ft; Math compound 5'-3" above road level), Fergusson leaf 442 (192 ft), Brown leaf 215 ('nearly 200 feet') found. Added mitra-r-1880 leaf 229 ('has a height of 192 feet'), fetched by the checker. See rulings.facts.height.
verdicts.revised_text: M.M. Ganguly surveyed the main tower before 1912. He found it about 65 m (215 ft) high, from road level to the top of its stone finial. Older books give about 58–61 m (192–200 ft).

verdicts.reason: Panigrahi leaf 284 (the three images named) and Fergusson leaf 441 ('his brother Balbhadra, and the sister Subhadhia') found. Only the naming is used; Fergusson's Buddhist reading is not. Ganguly vedi quote (leaf 483) not needed.

Ganguly leaf 497 ('Vimana (No. 4, plate XX. A) starts from a plinth') and leaf 498 ('It is a pancharatha dewl, the konakapaga showing 9 bhumis') found. The passage sits in Ganguly's Jagannath section (leaf 497 inner enclosure 420 x 315 ft; leaves 502-503 height survey of 'the vimana'; leaf 504 jagamohana doorways), and the tower is 'plastered all over with cement', matching Brown's account of the Puri tower. Attribution added.
verdicts.revised_text: According to M.M. Ganguly, the main shrine is a pancharatha deul (a tower whose walls step out in five vertical bands on each side).

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 215 ('appreciably larger building than the Lingaraja') and Panigrahi leaf 283 found. 'Eastern Ganga' changed to 'Ganga dynasty'.
verdicts.revised_text: The great temple of Jagannath at Puri, built by kings of the Ganga dynasty. Percy Brown called it a larger building than Bhubaneswar's Lingaraja.

verdicts.reason: Panigrahi leaf 282: 'from the Godaveri in the south to the river Hooghly in the north' and 'it is he who erected the present temple'.

Fergusson leaf 440 and Brown leaf 215 found. 'His dates are now outdated' is the researcher's judgement, not sourced (Fergusson's 1131 even falls inside Ganguly's window); replaced with Brown's own view.
verdicts.revised_text: Two scholars linked the temple to a victory. James Fergusson (1876) thought the Ganga kings built it at once to celebrate winning power. Percy Brown thought a victory pillar probably stood here first.

verdicts.reason: Ganguly leaves 485 and 487 found. Attributed to Ganguly; the Nagpur Prasasti edition itself was not opened.
verdicts.revised_text: M.M. Ganguly wrote that Puri was a holy place long before the present temple. He noted an inscription dated 1104 CE that already mentions Purushottama, a name of Puri's god.

verdicts.reason: Panigrahi leaf 277 (both quotes) and Ganguly leaf 487 found. Yayati pitfall: uncertain with note. Wording tightened to keep 'nothing can now be seen' as Panigrahi's.
verdicts.revised_text: Historian K.C. Panigrahi thought King Yayati I built an earlier Jagannath temple here in the 10th century CE. He wrote that nothing of it can be seen now.

verdicts.reason: Panigrahi leaf 283 found ('A presiding deity was to live in state as much as a king would do. He was to have an audience hall (Jagamohana), dancing hall...'). 'in Ganga times' not in the quote; removed.
verdicts.revised_text: K.C. Panigrahi explained that the temple's god was meant to live in state, like a king. So the god needed halls, such as an audience hall (jagamohana) and a dance hall (natamandira).

verdicts.reason: Brown leaves 215 and 11, Ganguly leaf 488 found. Whole account attributed to Brown (his 'appears to'); Ganguly's Purushottama Deva detail kept in the note only.
verdicts.revised_text: Percy Brown wrote that at first the temple had only the tower shrine and its porch hall. He thought the dance hall and offering hall were added in the 14th or 15th century CE.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 215 (sea air 'probably'; cement 'heavy and lifeless') and Ganguly leaf 497 ('plastered all over with') found; the cement continuation is on leaf 498. 'probably' restored.
verdicts.revised_text: Percy Brown thought sea air probably decayed the old stonework. Later repairs covered the tower with cement. Brown felt the cement made it look heavy.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 191 caption and Ganguly leaf 503 found. Leaf 503 carries the OCR margin note 'jsKunoluna ... oJjAsannath' (read as 'Jagamohana of Jagannath') beside the jagamohana plinth, so it is the Puri porch. First sentence ('Metal helps hold parts of the temple up') dropped as a generalisation.
verdicts.revised_text: A photograph caption in Percy Brown's book points out iron beams in the dance hall ceiling. In 1912, M.M. Ganguly described steel beams and old rails holding up the lowest layer of the porch hall's roof.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 215 ('four edifices in one alignment'; 310 feet) and Ganguly leaf 504 found. 310 ft = 94.5 m.

Ganguly leaves 494, 497; Brown leaves 215, 216; Fergusson leaf 442 found. 'Two high walls' removed: Brown speaks of three encircling walls ('Three Garlands', leaf 216) while Ganguly and Fergusson describe two. Inner-enclosure figures differ (420 x 315 vs 440 x 350 ft), so only the agreed outer-wall figures are used.
verdicts.revised_text: A high outer wall of laterite stone surrounds the temple grounds. It is about 6–7 m (20–24 ft) high and about 203 m by 195 m (665 by 640 ft).

verdicts.reason: Ganguly leaf 494 and Brown leaf 216 found. 'the most important' softened to Ganguly's 'considered the most important'.
verdicts.revised_text: The outer wall has a gate on each of its four sides. The eastern gate, thought of as the most important, is the Lion Gate. Two huge lion figures stand on either side of it.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 218, Ganguly leaves 488 and 184 found. Attributed to the two scholars; the 34 ft height (Ganguly leaf 494) kept in the note.
verdicts.revised_text: A tall stone pillar stands in front of the eastern gate. M.M. Ganguly and Percy Brown both say it was brought here from the Sun Temple at Konark.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 216 found. Single source; attributed.
verdicts.revised_text: Percy Brown wrote that some 30 or 40 smaller shrines stand around the main temple, inside the walls.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 215: '16 pillars in 4 rows of 4 each, the only real example of a hypostyle hall in Orissa'.

Quotes found (Panigrahi, OCR leaf 286 rather than 284). But it is one scholar's view on the origins of a living faith (Buddhism, Jainism, 'primitive cults'), overlapping claim 023. Sensitive: the human should rule whether a family site shows it.
Panigrahi leaf 284, Brown leaf 215, Fergusson leaf 441 found. Sensitive (Buddhist origin of living sacred images; Fergusson's wording dismissive). Not staged.
Brown leaf 215 found. Single source; attributed.
verdicts.revised_text: Percy Brown noted that the temple stands on raised ground. Its tall tower is a landmark across the flat land for many kilometres around.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 215 and Panigrahi leaf 283 found. Each view attributed; 'that great temple' changed to 'the builders of Lingaraja' as in the Lingaraja page (Panigrahi's 'them' is the earlier builders).
verdicts.revised_text: Percy Brown wrote that the temple follows the same plan as Bhubaneswar's Lingaraja temple. K.C. Panigrahi thought the Ganga kings wanted to match or outdo the builders of Lingaraja.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 215 found. Brown speaks of the contours and the shoulder, not only the top.
verdicts.revised_text: Percy Brown saw progress in its design. He found the tower's outline improved, with a more graceful curve at its shoulder than at Lingaraja.

verdicts.reason: Brown leaf 216: 'analogous to the arrangement of pylons and prakarams ... seems more than a coincidence'.

Ganguly quote found (search API gave leaf 584, ledger says 475; locator left unverified). Brown dates Puri c. 1100 (leaf 214) and compares Konark with it (leaf 218). Second sentence reworded so the carving is Ganguly's evidence, not proof.
verdicts.revised_text: The Puri temple is older than the Sun Temple at Konark. M.M. Ganguly pointed to a carving of Jagannath found in Konark's ruins as one sign of this.
